_comment: Biomes an abyss may not stand in, however deep the column is (Jonah, walking V3 on 2026-09-11:
'the caves are just playing havoc with it -- can we tweak deep water not to spawn in cave biomes,
since they're often considered deep enough even if the ocean itself isn't all that deep').
The abyss plane says WHERE deep water would be and the water table says WHETHER any stands there.
Neither can tell a trench floor from a flooded cavern: the default table is flat, so every space the
shape cut below the waterline is wet, and the plane is the waterline less eighty -- which in an Age
with caves is most of the underground. The biome is the one thing that already knows the difference,
because a cave biome is precisely the game saying 'you are underground here, not at sea'.
A tag rather than a list in code, for the reason `DeepWater.DEEP_WATER` is one: a pack that adds a
cave biome should be able to keep the abyss out of it without touching the mod.
`agesandtheart:abyss` is deliberately NOT here -- that is the biome the deep sea wears. `great_hall`
**Every id here must be a biome this pack actually ships.** A tag entry is a registry reference, so a
name with nothing behind it is left unbound and the BIOME registry fails to FREEZE -- which is a crash
at world load, not a warning. `great_halls` was written here first and did exactly that.
